title: Assam Student Found Dead by Andhra Railway Tracks After Reporting Harassment on Train
excerpt: Twenty-year-old Himashri Boro vanished from the Vivek Express in the early hours of October 6 after telling her family she felt unsafe; Assam's chief minister has written to his Andhra counterpart seeking a probe.
body:
• Himashri Boro, a 20-year-old B. Borooah College student from Guwahati, was found dead beside railway tracks in Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh, after disappearing from the Dibrugarh-bound Vivek Express in the early hours of October 6.
  • She had told her family she felt unsafe, saying she was surrounded by drunk men; her last message read “drunk men around me.” Her two bags were found intact in coach S2 when the train reached Guwahati.
  • Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has written to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu seeking a probe into her death, The Hindu reported. The Railway Protection Force and Government Railway Police are examining station CCTV footage and recording fellow passengers’ statements.
  • If you feel unsafe on an Indian train, her family’s first step is worth copying: they called railway helpline 139 to lodge a formal complaint, and the Rail Madad app lets passengers report harassment in real time. Sharing your coach and berth number with family before a night journey costs nothing.

Vanished in the night

The Dibrugarh-bound Vivek Express left Visakhapatnam on October 6 with Himashri Boro, a 20-year-old student of Guwahati’s B. Borooah College, in sleeper coach S2. She was traveling alone, returning early from a dance competition in Visakhapatnam because she had examinations coming up, according to her family. Around 2:39 a.m., she called home in distress.

https://x.com/DeccanHerald/status/2108564929154367771

She told her family she felt threatened by a group of men surrounding her berth. She sent a short video of the compartment to a friend. Then, according to her family, phone contact stopped abruptly.

When the train pulled into Guwahati, her two bags were still sitting in coach S2. She was not.

Body found hundreds of kilometres away

Her family contacted the Railways for help and lodged a formal complaint through helpline 139 and with the local Government Railway Police. Railway officials searched the general and reserved compartments but could not trace her, her family said. Her body was later recovered beside railway tracks near Tekkalipuram in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh — hundreds of kilometres from where she boarded.

“After getting on the train, she called me and another friend of hers, and told us that she was feeling uncomfortable in the coach. There were inebriated men all around, making her feel unsafe.”

— Boro’s sister-in-law, quoted by the Times of India

“We never heard back about her being safe. Her body has now been recovered near the railway tracks in Andhra Pradesh. Her two bags have been found intact inside the coach,” her sister-in-law said, demanding a detailed inquiry and strict action against those responsible.

Conflicting accounts, unanswered questions

Investigators are now piecing together her last hours. Station CCTV footage reviewed by police showed her rushing onto the train accompanied by an unidentified man, according to reports. Her family has raised suspicions about an acquaintance named Avinash who helped her board the train at Visakhapatnam.

Fellow passengers have given conflicting accounts about when she was last seen in her seat, with some suggesting she may have fallen from the moving train. A post-mortem and forensic examination are underway to establish the cause and circumstances of her death, with police teams in Andhra Pradesh and Assam coordinating the investigation.

Protests and a chief minister’s letter

The death has triggered protests. Students at B. Borooah College staged demonstrations demanding a high-level inquiry, accountability for railway personnel, and the immediate apprehension of suspects. The case has reignited a long-running debate over the safety of women on India’s long-distance trains, where sleeper coaches on overnight routes are often crowded and poorly monitored.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has written to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu seeking a probe into the student’s death, The Hindu reported.

What comes next

The Railway Protection Force and the Government Railway Police are recording statements from fellow passengers and examining CCTV footage from stations along the train’s route. The findings of the post-mortem examination will be central to determining whether Boro’s death was an accident, a fall, or something worse — the question her family, her college, and now two state governments are demanding an answer to.

image_caption: A representational image. The body of 20-year-old Himashri Boro was recovered beside railway tracks in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, after she disappeared from the Vivek Express.
nri_angle: Millions in the diaspora travel India's railways on visits home; the case is a stark reminder that night-train safety precautions — helpline 139, the Rail Madad app, and sharing berth details with family — matter for every traveler.
author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Himashri calls family, feels threatened by men.
Train arrives in Guwahati; her bags found, but she is missing.
Body discovered near railway tracks in Srikakulam.
